references.text: Repeats that the ransom was half a shekel (a beka) per person at the census, the same amount specified in Exodus 30:13.
Defines the sanctuary shekel as the standard for all valuations, the same unit of weight mentioned in Exodus 30:13.
Uses the sanctuary shekel of twenty gerahs as the payment standard for ransoms, identical to the weight given in Exodus 30:13.
Specifies the sanctuary shekel of twenty gerahs as the standard for ransoms for firstborns, the same unit of weight as in Exodus 30:13.
Confirms that a shekel is twenty gerahs, the same weight definition given in Exodus 30:13.
Nehemiah reinstates an annual temple tax of one-third of a shekel, based on the principle of the temple contribution from Exodus 30:13.
Jesus pays the temple tax (didrachma), which was the Greek equivalent of the half shekel required in Exodus 30:13.
